Six cells form a three-box rectangle on digits 1, 3 and 5. If r3c1 used 1 or 5, both selected columns would contain these three digits. Swapping the columns within the rectangle would give a second solution. Remove 1 and 5 from r3c1.
BUG+1 found.

The bases row 1, column 1 mix a row with a column. Without a fin, digit 1 fills the covers column 3, box 3. The target sees every fin, so remove 1 from r7c3.

Aligned Triplet Exclusion: chain of 3 ALS linked by shared value 6.

If r1c7 were 7, row 1, column 7 and box 3 could not all be filled: every boundary signature has a Hall-deficient cell set. Therefore remove 7 from r1c7.
Combine these exactly-one requirements: +1 × (cell r5c8). If r5c8=1 is false, the remaining sum would be 1, outside its possible interval [0, 0]. Place 1 in r5c8.
Place 9 at r9c5: the opposite assumption leaves a selected native peer graph with no candidate-respecting coloring. Every case is covered by the checked refutation tree.
Assume r7c9 is 7. Follow only this digit's strong and weak implications. The assumption leaves row 6 without a position for 7. Remove 7 from r7c9.
